To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed a logic-based approach to access control that allows dynamic updates and provides a sound and complete policy evaluation mechanism.
we have implemented a logic-based access control system that is able to perform authorisation evaluations and policy updates.

(i) a logic-based approach is suitable for the representation and evaluation of dynamic access control policies; (ii) the Stable Model semantics is suitable for the evaluation of access control policies; and (iii) the use of the Stable Model semantics for access control policy evaluation allows the use of a wide variety of logic programming languages and tools
In summary, our research is concerned with

(i) The design of a logic-based access control language $\mathcal L$; (ii) The design of an algorithm to translate $\mathcal L$, and its associated constraints, to a form suitable for the Stable Model semantics; (iii) The implementation of the algorithm and the development of the PolicyUpdater system; (iv) The evaluation of PolicyUpdater in a number of case studies, and a comparison of the performance of PolicyUpdater to other systems.

a logic-based language for access control is well-suited to dynamic policy updates and that the Stable Model semantics is a good choice for the evaluation of such updates.
